items.prompt: 2 million app events per second must reach billing, fraud detection and a data lake. A new recommendations team will join next month and wants the last 5 days too.
items.why: Very high volume, several independent consumer groups and replay of past days → a retained, partitioned log.

items.prompt: Each uploaded video needs one transcoding job. Jobs take 1–20 minutes, failed jobs retry after 5 minutes, and premium users' jobs go first.
items.why: Per-job acks, delayed retries and priorities are task-queue features. In a Kafka partition, one slow job blocks every record behind it.

items.prompt: Every status change of an order (created, paid, shipped) must be processed in order for that order, at 300k updates per second across all orders.
items.why: Per-key ordering at scale → partition by order_id. Order holds inside a partition, and the partitions give the parallelism.

items.prompt: From a stream of page views, compute the number of unique visitors per page in 1-minute tumbling windows, handling events that arrive up to 30 s late.
items.why: Windows, late events and aggregation are computation on the stream. Kafka would carry the events, but it doesn't compute anything.

items.prompt: The search index must reflect every insert, update and delete in the products table within seconds, without changing the application code that writes to the table.
items.why: The key requirement is getting changes out of the database's own log without touching the writers. That's CDC. Kafka is usually only the transport.

items.prompt: A consumer bug corrupted the analytics tables for the last 3 days. After the fix, the team wants to recompute them from the original events.
items.why: Replay: reset the group's offsets to 3 days ago and reprocess. That only works if a retained log still holds the events.

items.prompt: A small internal tool sends a welcome email after sign-up, about 200 per day. The team wants it out of the request path.
items.why: Simple async work at tiny volume, with no replay or fan-out. Any queue works, and running a Kafka cluster for it is overkill.
